\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اندھیرا} (andherā)}{اندھیرا (andherā)}]{\ur{اندھیرا} (andherā) — darkness}

\label{lesson:UR-C292-andhera}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to cave in, then the Urdu for to be trapped under.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اندھیرا}}
\textbf{\ur{اندھیرا}} — \emph{andherā} — \textquotedblleft{}darkness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{شہر} \ur{میں} \ur{اندھیرا} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shahr meṅ andherā thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The city was dark.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اندھیرا}} (\emph{andherā}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{andhakāra}, \textquotedblleft{}darkness\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 386), where CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{ãdherā}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{andherā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{andherā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shahr meṅ andherā thā.} — The city was dark.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to cave in, then the Urdu for to be trapped under, then say \emph{andherā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{اندھیرا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Darkness\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{گرجنا} (garajnā)}{گرجنا (garajnā)}]{\ur{گرجنا} (garajnā) — to thunder; to roar}

\label{lesson:UR-C292-garajna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to be trapped under, then the Urdu for darkness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{گرجنا}}
\textbf{\ur{گرجنا}} — \emph{garajnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to thunder; to roar\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{رات} \ur{کو} \ur{بادل} \ur{گرج} \ur{رہے} \ur{تھے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rāt ko bādal garaj rahe the.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The clouds were thundering in the night.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{شیر} \ur{گرج} \ur{اٹھا}, \emph{voh sher garaj uṭhā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{gárjati}, \textquotedblleft{}thunders, roars\textquotedblright{}, where CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{gājnā} (CDIAL 4046); \textbf{\ur{گرجنا}} keeps the Sanskrit shape closer. Clouds \textbf{\ur{گرجتے} \ur{ہیں}}, and so does a lion.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{garajnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rāt ko bādal garaj rahe the.} — The clouds were thundering in the night.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to be trapped under, then the Urdu for darkness, then say \emph{garajnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{گرجنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To thunder; to roar\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{چمکنا} (chamaknā)}{چمکنا (chamaknā)}]{\ur{چمکنا} (chamaknā) — to flash; to gleam}

\label{lesson:UR-C292-chamakna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for darkness, then the Urdu for to thunder.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{چمکنا}}
\textbf{\ur{چمکنا}} — \emph{chamaknā} — \textquotedblleft{}to flash; to gleam\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{آسمان} \ur{میں} \ur{بجلی} \ur{چمکی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āsmān meṅ bijlī chamkī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Lightning flashed in the sky.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{بجلی} \ur{چمکی}, \emph{voh bijlī chamkī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{چمکنا}} (\emph{chamaknā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{camaknā}, \textquotedblleft{}to glitter\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*camakka}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 4676).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تباہی} (tabāhī)}{تباہی (tabāhī)}]{\ur{تباہی} (tabāhī) — destruction; havoc}

\label{lesson:UR-C292-tabahi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to thunder, then the Urdu for to flash.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تباہی}}
\textbf{\ur{تباہی}} — \emph{tabāhī} — \textquotedblleft{}destruction; havoc\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{طوفان} \ur{سے} \ur{ہر} \ur{جگہ} \ur{تباہی} \ur{ہوئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tūfān se har jagah tabāhī huī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The storm caused destruction everywhere.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تباہی}} (\emph{tabāhī}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{tabāhī}, \textquotedblleft{}ruin\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{tabāh}, \textquotedblleft{}ruined\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to thunder, then the Urdu for to flash, then say \emph{tabāhī} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اثر} (asar)}{اثر (asar)}]{\ur{اثر} (asar) — an effect}

\label{lesson:UR-C292-asar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to flash, then the Urdu for destruction.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اثر}}
\textbf{\ur{اثر}} — \emph{asar} — \textquotedblleft{}an effect\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{طوفان} \ur{کا} \ur{اثر} \ur{دو} \ur{دن} \ur{رہا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tūfān kā asar do din rahā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The storm's effects lasted two days.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اثر}} (\emph{asar}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{athar}, \textquotedblleft{}a trace, a mark left behind\textquotedblright{}. Urdu says its middle letter as \emph{s}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{asar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{asar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tūfān kā asar do din rahā.} — The storm's effects lasted two days.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to flash, then the Urdu for destruction, then say \emph{asar} again
\end{itemize}
